title: The Adolescent Brain: Pruning, Myelination, and the Prefrontal Cortex — A Second Chance
summary: Adolescence = a second window for brain growth (UNICEF): (1) Synaptic pruning — the brain retains what is used and neglects what is not. (2) Myelination — speeds up signals, finally reaching the prefrontal cortex. (3) Prefrontal cortex (PFC) — decision-making, planning, impulse control — completes in the 20s. The interpretation: your adolescent is not "broken"; their brain is rewiring. The opportunity: what they practice now (sports, knowledge, art, *salah*, leadership) becomes ingrained for life.
try_this: This week: choose together one skill your child wishes to develop — plan: 30 minutes daily for 30 days. Record: how did performance/confidence change?
reflection_prompts: Did they feel a difference after 30 days?
